transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thanks. Well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that... I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. 

Between my work and my side projects, there's just a lot on my plate right now—patent notes I need to review, prep for a workshop, some gallery deadlines, and just the daily team decisions I have to make as a developer. It's all just jumbled together. Whenever I sit down to work, I end up just starting on whatever is loudest or most urgent in that exact second, instead of focusing on what actually matters. It's getting really frustrating, and I just need to figure out how to get a handle on it.
Do you often feel anxious or overwhelmed by all these tasks and responsibilities?

I'm not sure I'd call it anxiety. I don't really feel panicked or nervous about it, if that's what you mean. 

It's more just... frustrating. I haven't really noticed feeling overwhelmed in an emotional way, I guess. It's really just annoying that I know what needs to be done, but I can't seem to get everything lined up and actually focus on the right things. So, no, not really anxious. Just tired of spinning my wheels.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or situations because of feeling overwhelmed by your responsibilities?

No, I wouldn't say I avoid them. Like I mentioned, it's not really a feeling of being overwhelmed that stops me. I don't look at a big task and run away from it. 

It's more that... I just get sidetracked. I'll sit at my desk fully intending to work on the workshop prep, but then I see an email from a team member and I just pivot to that instead. So I'm still working, and I'm not hiding from my responsibilities. I'm just not doing the ones I actually sat down to do.
Do you often find your mind wandering when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yeah, definitely. It happens all the time. 

I'll be right in the middle of writing a piece of code, and if Slack pings, or a browser tab flashes... or honestly, even if just a visual idea for one of my side projects pops into my head, I completely lose the thread of what I was doing. I can easily spend twenty minutes just going down some unrelated design rabbit hole before I realize I've completely stopped working on the code I was supposed to be writing.
Do you ever find yourself so intensely focused on a task that you lose track of time and forget about everything else?

No, not really. I don't think I ever get that kind of intense focus. 

Like I said, my problem is usually the opposite. I can't stay on one thing for very long before something else catches my attention. I never really get so absorbed in a task that I lose track of time or forget about everything else around me. I'm usually too easily distracted for that to happen.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about your inability to focus or complete tasks?

No, I wouldn't say I feel worthless or guilty. It's frustrating, sure. I mean, I know I should be getting certain things done, and it's annoying when I realize I've wasted an hour on something completely unrelated. But I don't beat myself up over it or feel like a failure. It's just... a hassle I deal with. I know I'm capable of doing the work, I just struggle to stay on a straight path to finish it.
Have you always had difficulty staying focused, or is this a relatively new challenge for you?

It's definitely always been there. Looking back, I had the exact same issues in grade school. I remember my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but spent too much time daydreaming. I was constantly forgetting to turn in assignments that I had actually finished, or I'd just completely lose my homework folders. So, yeah, this was happening long before I was even a teenager. It's just always been how my brain works, I guess.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah, I do. Especially at work. When I'm on long design calls, I start to feel this... pressure building up in my body to just get up and move. I usually end up pacing around my office, or I'll keep shifting from chair to chair, even when I’m trying my best to look focused on the screen. It's just really hard to sit completely still for that long.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends, family, or coworkers due to your difficulty staying focused or getting things done?

Yeah, mostly at work with my coworkers. It's actually started to damage my professional reputation. I, uh... I recently missed a pretty important patent filing checkpoint because I just lost track of the steps. And then we had this difficult architecture review, and because I wasn't fully prepared or focused, it really didn't go well. It actually left my collaborators questioning whether I can handle leading the larger project we're supposed to be doing. So, yeah, it's definitely causing some real problems for me professionally.
Have you experienced any difficulties in your personal relationships with friends or family due to your struggles with focus or follow-through?

Not really, no. I mean, my wife sometimes gets annoyed if I forget to take out the trash or if I zone out when she's talking about her day, but... it's nothing major. We've been married a long time, so I think she's just used to it by now. My friends don't seem to mind either. It's really just work where it's causing actual problems.
Have you ever been fired or demoted from a job due to your difficulties with focus or follow-through?

No, I haven't been fired or demoted. I mean, like I said, it's definitely causing some tension and people are questioning my reliability right now, but it hasn't come to anything official like losing my job or getting knocked down a level. I've managed to hold onto my position so far.
Have you noticed any problems in your personal relationships, such as with your wife or friends, that you think are directly because of your difficulty staying focused or following through on things?

I think we just touched on that, actually. But, uh, no, not really. Like I mentioned a minute ago, my wife gets a little annoyed sometimes if I forget to do a chore around the house or if I tune out during a conversation, but it hasn't caused any real problems between us. And my friends haven't said anything or seemed bothered. So, no, nothing major on the personal side.
Have you ever lost a friend due to your inability to follow through on plans or maintain focus in social interactions?
No, never. I've never lost a friend over anything like that. Like I said, my friends really don't seem bothered by it. It's just work where this is an issue.
Have you ever had to significantly adjust your work or personal life to accommodate your difficulties with focus and follow-through?

No, I haven't really done anything like that. I mean, I haven't made any major changes or rearranged my life around it. I just try to push through my work day as best I can and deal with the delays as they happen. So, no, no big adjustments to how I live or work.
Have you ever had to turn down a social invitation or a work opportunity because of your difficulties with focus or follow-through?

No, I haven't. I've never turned down a project at work because of this. I just... I take the work, and then I end up struggling to get it done on time. And socially, no, I still go out when I'm invited. So it hasn't really stopped me from accepting things, it just makes actually doing them a bit harder once I'm committed.
Do you think your difficulties with focus and follow-through are affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah, I think it is. Mostly because it's really starting to damage my reputation at work. I actually missed a patent filing checkpoint recently, which was a pretty big deal. And then... we had this difficult architecture review, and it didn't go well. It actually left my collaborators questioning whether I can even lead the larger project. So, knowing that my colleagues are losing faith in me because I can't keep on top of things... yeah, that definitely affects my quality of life.
Do you often interrupt others when they are speaking or finish their sentences for them?
No, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty quiet when other people are talking. I don't really jump in or try to finish their sentences for them. I just let them say what they need to say.
Do you often have difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations or lines?

No, not really. I mean, if I'm at the store or something, I just wait in line. It doesn't really bother me. And with conversations... like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm more likely to just sit back and listen. I don't feel any kind of urge to jump ahead or rush people. So, no, waiting my turn is usually fine.
Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder or taken any medication for attention problems?
No, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that. And I haven't taken any medication for attention issues, either. This is really the first time I'm talking to a doctor about any of this.
Do you think your difficulties with restlessness and fidgeting are as significant as your problems with staying focused?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really struggle with restlessness or fidgeting at all. I sit at a desk most of the day for my job, and sitting still is fine. It's really just... the focus. Trying to keep my mind on the actual work in front of me is the hard part. So, no, the focus is definitely the main problem, not restlessness.
